headline: High: Dify’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can conflict with a local-only game agent, while prompt-injection and leakage risks stay limited by the game agent’s no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and tool outputs, and it has broad filesystem/network capabilities; godot_rl_agents exposes no shared channel, no MCP, and no browser/clipboard surface. Without a documented bridge, prompt injection is only plausible through unusual manual copy-paste or file handoff, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Dify output into godot_rl_agents prompts or configs
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or message queue outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable manual copy-paste between agent outputs and agent inputs
Use a human review step before forwarding any generated text
Rename or segregate shared files to prevent accidental reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, but godot_rl_agents has no data classes and no network egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated cloud principal, so leakage is limited to accidental local exposure rather than automatic exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory or uploaded file set
IF Dify conversation logs are exported into a location godot_rl_agents can read
mitigations: Store Dify artifacts in a separate directory
Restrict file permissions on any shared host
Avoid placing secrets in uploaded knowledge-base files
Purge conversation logs before sharing outputs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; godot_rl_agents is local-only and appears non-mutating. There is no evidence of locking or coordination, so if both are run against the same mutable directory or resource, Dify can overwrite or race with the other agent even though godot_rl_agents itself lacks write/network overlap.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory
IF Dify tools are allowed to modify shared artifacts without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Make shared resources read-only for godot_rl_agents
Check for file locks before Dify writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate tool outputs and workflow artifacts that a downstream agent could treat as authoritative, while godot_rl_agents has no documented verification or critique surface in the profile. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium: a bad Dify output could cascade if the game agent consumes it as input.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents consumes Dify-produced text or files as input
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Insert a validation step before reuse of Dify outputs
Require schema checks on any transferred artifacts
Have a human review high-impact outputs
Limit Dify outputs to non-authoritative drafts
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, model-provider keys, and tool credentials, while godot_rl_agents shows no sensitive data classes or residency constraints. No mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is mainly about Dify’s own handling of sensitive content rather than a pairwise breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Dify knowledge bases or logs
IF those artifacts are then exported into a jurisdiction or system with stricter retention rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Dify
Shorten log retention settings
Separate secrets from knowledge-base uploads
Review export destinations before sharing artifacts
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
